attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) to route between lan-a (node1<->node2, 10.60.10.0/24) and lan-b (node1<->node3, 10.60.20.0/24) by creating opt1/opt2 interfaces on vtnet1/vtnet2, assigning static routed IPs on node2/node3 via NetworkManager, and adding a single OPNsense port alias "node3_svc_ports" (8080, 8443, 9000) referenced by one firewall pass rule permitting node2->node3 TCP traffic on that alias (not one rule per port). Also fixed a secondary blocker: node3's local firewalld was rejecting the forwarded traffic even though pf correctly forwarded it; opened the three ports in firewalld on node3. Verified the three named ports work, an out-of-set port (9999) stays blocked, and the reverse direction (node3->node2) is blocked by default-deny. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time; boot identity change was proven via kern.boottime (node1, FreeBSD) and /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id (node2/node3, Linux), and post-restart the alias, pf rule, interface addressing, static routes, and firewalld port openings all persisted, with a full end-to-end functional re-test passing after the last restart.
